extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting to the Journal of the Medical Library Association (JMLA); health sciences librarians and researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Journal policy and guidance requiring use of the CRediT (Contributor Role Taxonomy) vocabulary in Author Contribution statements for specified JMLA manuscript types, with definitions of the 14 contributor roles. Useful for authors preparing contribution statements and for editors verifying role attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include Author Contribution statement using CRediT
rubrics_metrics.description: As of July 1, 2021, Knowledge Synthesis, Original Investigations, Case Reports, Special Papers, and Virtual Projects manuscripts submitted to JMLA must contain an Author Contribution statement that uses CRediT to specify the role(s) played by each author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a CRediT-style Author Contributions statement at submission/publication. Example format: 'Brittany Eagleton: Methodology; investigation; writing—review and editing. John Tramos: Conceptualization; methodology; investigation; software; data curation; formal analysis; visualization; writing—original draft.' Multiple roles may be listed per author; use the standardized role labels from the taxonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas; formulation or evolution of overarching research goals and aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this CRediT role when an author contributed to the original idea or overall aims of the project. Include as part of the Author Contribution statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Management activities to annotate (produce metadata), scrub data and maintain research data (including software code, where it is necessary for interpreting the data itself) for initial use and later re-use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to authors who prepared, cleaned, or otherwise managed datasets or code necessary to interpret the data. Include in Author Contribution statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of statistical, mathematical, computational, or other formal techniques to analyze or synthesize study data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for authors who performed statistical or computational analyses or synthesized data. List alongside other roles as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of the financial support for the project leading to this publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to authors who obtained grants or other funding that supported the work. Note that funding acquisition alone may not satisfy authorship criteria per ICMJE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting a research and investigation process, specifically performing the experiments, or data/evidence collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for authors involved in hands-on data collection, experiments, or other empirical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Development or design of methodology; creation of models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to authors who designed the methodological approach or created models used in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and coordination responsibility for the research activity planning and execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for authors who managed project logistics, coordination, timelines, and administrative oversight relevant to the research activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of study materials, reagents, materials, patients, laboratory samples, animals, instrumentation, computing resources, or other analysis tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to contributors who provided essential resources or materials. Be mindful that providing resources alone may not constitute authorship under ICMJE but should be acknowledged and/or credited via CRediT as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming, software development; designing computer programs; implementation of the computer code and supporting algorithms; testing of existing code components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for authors who wrote or developed code, algorithms, or software tools central to the research and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight and leadership responsibility for the research activity planning and execution, including mentorship external to the core team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to senior authors or supervisors who provided leadership and oversight throughout the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification, whether as a part of the activity or separate, of the overall replication/reproducibility of results/experiments and other research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for authors who performed verification, replication checks, or reproducibility assessments of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation, or presentation of the published work, specifically visualization/data presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to authors who prepared figures, tables, or other visual representations of data for the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing—original draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation, or presentation of the published work, specifically writing the initial draft (including substantive translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for authors who wrote the first draft of the manuscript or performed substantive initial writing tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing—review & editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work by those from the original research group, specifically critical review, commentary or revision—including pre- or post-publication stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to authors who contributed to revising, editing, or critically reviewing manuscript drafts at any stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ICMJE guidance to determine authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on determining authorship is provided by the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE), which defines roles and responsibilities for authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICMJE offers criteria for who merits authorship; CRediT provides standardized role labels but does not replace ICMJE authorship criteria. Authors and teams should use ICMJE recommendations together with CRediT to decide inclusion and order of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example Author Contributions formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Author Contributions statement demonstrating how to list authors and their CRediT roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the example format provided: 'LastName FirstName: Role1; Role2; Role3.' Use semicolons to separate roles, list only applicable standardized role labels, and include all contributing authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of CRediT and alternative/expanded ontologies
rubrics_metrics.description: CRediT does not currently describe all roles that librarians play in contributing to publications; the Contributor Role Ontology is an effort to expand contributor role terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize CRediT's limitations for some librarian-specific roles; consider Contributor Role Ontology or similar expanded vocabularies for more granular attribution, while using CRediT as the immediate standard for JMLA submissions.
